transcript.text: theres a funny smell from my oven when its on

That smell is often caused by dust burning off on new elements or a loose mains connection at the back of the oven overheating. It could also be normal if it’s a brand-new appliance, but we should rule out electrical issues first. Please switch the oven off and unplug it from the wall to make it safe. Then check behind the unit for any signs of melting plastic, charring, or discoloured wires where the power cable enters. If you see no damage there, let me know what you found so we can look at other possibilities.

its a belling, about 12 years old. cooker is too heavy for me to pull out from the wall to look behind. the smell is more like hot plastic or electrical burning, from the back/lower bit not inside the oven. also the cooker switch looks a bit brown at one corner and felt warm

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. The warm switch and brown corner suggest a loose connection at the mains terminal block is overheating, which can also cause that hot plastic smell from the lower back of the oven. This is a serious fire hazard because high resistance in the wiring creates intense heat. You must stop using the cooker immediately until a qualified engineer has checked it safely. Please do not try to move the heavy appliance yourself or attempt any repairs on the internal wiring. Leave it switched off and isolated from the power supply for now.
